title: Anchor probe eval and automated safe-rollback playbook for batching/caching changes
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Summary: Build an automated evaluation and rollback playbook that uses small, representative 'anchor probe' sets plus lightweight online checks to validate batching and KV cache recommendation changes before and during rollout. The goal is to reduce per-token cost by applying batching/cache configs safely while keeping measurable quality regressions below strict acceptance thresholds. This ticket covers the eval harness, acceptance thresholds, mini-canary lanes, shadow-apply experiments, and an automated rollback trigger set tied to both offline probe regressions and live-sample drift signals.
acceptance_criteria: Anchor probe suite constructed with 8k prompts representing 4 workload classes (chat, summarization, instruction, short Q&A)
Automated offline evaluation runs within CI that compare baseline vs candidate config and compute semantic match and token-KL metrics
Statistical test: paired bootstrap with 95% CI implemented; candidate accepted only if semantic-match drop <= 0.5% absolute and token-KL <= 0.02
Mini-canary lanes deploy candidate to 1% production traffic with shadow-apply for 24h before commit to 10%
Automated rollback triggers if BOTH anchor-probe offline fail AND live canary drift > threshold, or if live error-rate increase > 3x baseline
Playbook documented with runbook links, required approvals, and manual override instructions
testing_plan: Offline: run anchor probes nightly against candidate configs; store per-prompt metrics in eval DB
Shadow-apply: route 5% of requests to runtime with candidate config but return baseline response; compute divergence metrics in parallel
Mini-canary: after shadow-stable, route 1% (non-critical tokens) to candidate path with monitoring and canary logging enabled
A/B drift checks: sample live traffic and compute rolling 1h window semantic similarity, token-KL, latency 95th percentile, and downstream error rates
Post-apply watch: 72h focused monitoring with automated alerts to SLO owners and rollback automation ready
rollout_plan: Step 0: Author PR with recommended batching/cache config and experiment metadata (config id, reason, estimate) - link to PR required
Step 1: CI offline anchor-probe run (must pass acceptance thresholds)
Step 2: Shadow-apply for 24h (must show no meaningful divergence in live samples)
Step 3: Mini-canary 1% for 24h (alerting enabled). If stable, proceed to 10% for 48h
Step 4: Ramp to 50% over 3 days with autoscaling params pinned. Finalize at target capacity after 7d of stable metrics
At any step, automated rollback may trigger; manual rollback procedures documented in runbook
metrics_thresholds: Semantic-match (custom embedding-similarity metric) drop allowed <= 0.005 absolute (0.5%) on anchor probes
Token-level KL divergence allowed <= 0.02 between baseline and candidate across sample set
Latency p95 must not increase by more than 15ms on average for observed request classes
Error-rate (5xx or model-fail) must not increase by >3x baseline or exceed 0.5% absolute
Cost/unit expected reduction must be >= 4% for candidate to be considered
rollback_playbook: - Offline fail: anchor-probe acceptance criteria failed for candidate in CI
- Live drift: rolling 1h semantic-match drop > 0.01 AND token-KL > 0.03
- Error surge: live error-rate > 3x baseline or > 0.5% absolute
- Immediately route traffic back to pinned baseline config (fast path rollback),
- Freeze all further rollout ramps and mute autoscaler changes from the candidate pool
- Emit incident to #runtime-oncall with contextual links (PR, eval run id, dashboards)
- Run expanded anchor-probe suite and human review on flagged prompts
- Triage kernel/hardware interactions if latency regressions observed
- Postmortem and next-step checklist within 5 working days

open_questions: Should we enforce per-customer holdout for enterprise tenants that have strict SLAs? Current plan adds a manual opt-out but not programmatic holdout
Do we use a single global acceptance threshold or per-workload thresholds (chat vs summarization)? Current default is global to simplify automation
What is the retention policy for probe results and how long should we keep historical CI outputs for regression attribution?
